ideas: The bishop on c4 targets f7, Black's weakest square early on.
Prepare d4 with c3: a broad pawn center is White's long-term goal.
In the slow Pianissimo (d3), maneuver Nbd2-f1-g3 and play h3 to stop ...Bg4.
Castle early, put a rook on e1 and keep the e4 pawn solid.
Punish early queen sorties and knight jumps like ...Nd4 by simply developing and trading.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano 4...Qe7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Qe7 {The old Giuoco Piano: guarding e5.} 5.d4 Bb6 6.O-O Nf6 7.Re1 d6 8.h3 {Ideal setup: strong center, no ...Bg4.}

lines.name: Pianissimo 5...d5?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3 d5?! {A premature central break.} 6.exd5 Nxd5 7.O-O O-O 8.Re1 {The e5 pawn is under fire.}

lines.name: Two Knights 4...d5?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 d5?! {Opening the center too early.} 5.exd5 Nxd5 6.O-O Be7 7.Re1 {Hitting e5 and planning d4.}

lines.name: 3...Nge7?! and the f7 attack
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nge7?! {Blocks the bishop and leaves f7 weak.} 4.Ng5 {Hitting f7 again.} d5 5.exd5 Nxd5? 6.Nxf7! Kxf7 7.Qf3+ Ke6 8.Nc3 {A Fried Liver-style attack.}

lines.name: 3...h6?! slow move
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 h6?! {Too slow.} 4.d4 {Use the time to grab the center.} exd4 5.Nxd4 {White has a big lead in development.}

ideas: Pressure the c6 knight — it defends e5.
Retreat Ba4-b3 when attacked and keep the bishop aiming at f7.
Play c3 and d4 to build an ideal center; h3 stops ...Bg4.
The knight often travels b1-d2-f1-g3 to support a kingside attack.
Against gambits like the Marshall or Schliemann, accept material and defend calmly.

lines.name: Closed: Zaitsev 9...Bb7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O-O Be7 6.Re1 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.c3 O-O 9.h3 Bb7 {The Zaitsev: pressure on e4.} 10.d4 Re8 11.Nbd2 Bf8 12.a4 {Main line: queenside pressure.}

lines.name: Closed: Breyer 9...Nb8
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O-O Be7 6.Re1 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.c3 O-O 9.h3 Nb8 {The Breyer: the knight reroutes to d7.} 10.d4 Nbd7 11.Nbd2 Bb7 12.Bc2 Re8 13.Nf1 Bf8 14.Ng3 {The classic maneuver is complete.}

lines.name: Arkhangelsk 5...b5 6...Bb7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O-O b5 6.Bb3 Bb7 {The Arkhangelsk: active bishops.} 7.Re1 Bc5 8.c3 d6 9.d4 Bb6 10.Bg5 {Pinning and pressuring e5.}

lines.name: Møller 5...Bc5
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O-O Bc5 {The active Møller.} 6.c3 b5 7.Bb3 d6 8.d4 Bb6 9.a4 {Pressure on the queenside and e5.}

lines.name: Smyslov 3...g6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 g6 {Fianchetto defense.} 4.c3 {Preparing d4 against the g7 bishop.} a6 5.Ba4 d6 6.d4 Bd7 7.O-O Bg7 8.Re1 {A solid center.}

lines.name: Berlin 4...d6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 Nf6 4.O-O d6 {A solid, Steinitz-like Berlin.} 5.d4 Bd7 6.Nc3 Be7 7.Re1 exd4 8.Nxd4 {Typical space advantage.}

ideas: Open the center immediately with 3.d4 and develop quickly.
The knight on d4 is centralized; trade it on c6 when Black's pieces target it.
In the Mieses, push e5 to kick the f6 knight and grab space.
Watch f2: ...Bc5 and ...Qf6 or ...Qh4 aim at it.

lines.name: Classical 6...bxc6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Bc5 5.Nxc6 Qf6 6.Qd2 bxc6 {Recapturing toward the center.} 7.Bd3 Ne7 8.O-O O-O 9.Nc3 {Quick development and a solid center.}

lines.name: Mieses 8...Nb6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nxc6 bxc6 6.e5 Qe7 7.Qe2 Nd5 8.c4 Nb6 9.Nd2 Qe6 10.b3 a5 11.Bb2 {Main line: e5 is a thorn in Black's side.}

lines.name: 4...Qf6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 Qf6 {Hitting d4.} 5.Be3 Bc5 6.c3 Nge7 7.Bc4 O-O 8.O-O {Calm development; the queen on f6 will become a target.}

lines.name: 3...d6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 d6 {Holding e5.} 4.Bb5 Bd7 5.Nc3 Nf6 6.O-O Be7 7.Re1 exd4 8.Nxd4 {A Steinitz Ruy Lopez with free play for White.}

lines.name: 4...g6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 exd4 4.Nxd4 g6 5.Nc3 Bg7 6.Be3 Nf6 7.Nxc6 bxc6 8.e5 {Kicking the knight.} Ng8 9.Bd4 {A strong bind on the dark squares.}

ideas: Ng5 plus Bc4 doubles the attack on f7.
After ...d5 exd5, never let Black regain the pawn cheaply.
If Black plays the natural ...Nxd5, the Fried Liver sacrifice Nxf7 exposes the king.
In the main line, keep the extra pawn and finish development before Black's activity grows.

lines.name: Main line 10...Qd4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2 h6 9.Nf3 e4 10.Ne5 Qd4 {Attacking the knight and f2.} 11.f4 Bc5 12.Rf1 {Everything is protected.}

lines.name: Fried Liver: 7...Kg8?? mate
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Nxd5? 6.Nxf7! Kxf7 7.Qf3+ Kg8?? {Walking into a pin.} 8.Bxd5+ Qxd5 9.Qxd5+ Be6 10.Qxe6# {Checkmate.}

lines.name: 4...h6? 5.Nxf7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 h6? {Ignoring the threat.} 5.Nxf7 Qe7 6.Nxh8 {Winning the exchange and a pawn.}

ideas: Give the f-pawn to open the f-file and build a big center with d4.
After ...exf4, Nf3 stops ...Qh4+; then regain f4 with Bxf4 or undermine it with h4/g3.
Castle quickly: the open f-file plus a rook on f1 targets f7.
Against counter-strikes with ...d5, keep development flowing — tempo matters more than pawns.

lines.name: Kieseritzky 5...d6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 g5 4.h4 g4 5.Ne5 d6 6.Nxg4 Nf6 7.Nxf6+ Qxf6 8.Nc3 {Rapid development and a strong center.}

lines.name: Becker 3...h6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 h6 {The Becker Defense.} 4.d4 g5 5.h4 Bg7 6.hxg5 hxg5 7.Rxh8 Bxh8 8.g3 {Undermining the f4 pawn.}

lines.name: Falkbeer 3...c6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 d5 3.exd5 c6 4.Nc3 exf4 5.Nf3 {Back to a King's Gambit with extra development.}

lines.name: 3...Nc6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Nf3 Nc6 4.d4 d5 5.exd5 Qxd5 6.Nc3 Qa5 7.Bxf4 {White regains the pawn with a nice position.}

ideas: Develop Nc3 first, keeping f4 in reserve.
The Vienna Gambit (f4) opens the f-file and aims for e5 with a space edge.
Against ...Nc6/...Bc5 setups, Bc4 and Qg4 hit g7 and f7.
Castle and bring a rook to f1 once the f-file opens.

lines.name: Vienna Gambit 5...Bg4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.f4 d5 4.fxe5 Nxe4 5.Nf3 Bg4 6.Qe2 Nxc3 7.dxc3 c6 8.Bf4 {A lead in development and the e5 wedge.}

lines.name: Vienna Gambit 3...d6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6 3.f4 d6 {Solid but passive.} 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.Bb5 Bd7 6.d3 {A comfortable King's Gambit Declined.}

lines.name: 2...Nc6 3...Nf6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Bc5 5.f4 d6 6.Nf3 {A Vienna/King's Gambit hybrid with pressure on f7.}

lines.name: 2...Nc6 4...g6?
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.Qg4 g6? {Weakens the dark squares.} 5.Qf3 {Double attack on f7.}

ideas: Sacrifice pawns for a huge development lead and two bishops raking the kingside.
Aim the bishops at f7 and g7; open lines matter more than material.
If Black returns material with ...d5, simplify into a comfortable position.

lines.name: 4...Nf6 5.Nxc3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Bc4 Nf6 5.Nxc3 Nc6 6.Nf3 Bb4 7.O-O {A Göring-style setup with great activity.}

lines.name: 5...Bb4+
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Bc4 cxb2 5.Bxb2 Bb4+ 6.Nc3 Nf6 7.Ne2 O-O 8.O-O {Two pawns down, but every piece is active.}

lines.name: 3...Qe7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3 Qe7 4.cxd4 Qxe4+ 5.Be3 {Development with tempo coming: Nc3 and Nf3.}

ideas: Give the b-pawn to gain time: c3 and d4 follow with tempo on the bishop.
Qb3 and Bc4 together hammer f7.
Ba3 can stop Black from castling.
Rapid development and open central files are your compensation.

lines.name: Accepted 5...Bc5
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.b4 Bxb4 5.c3 Bc5 6.d4 exd4 7.O-O d6 8.cxd4 Bb6 9.Nc3 {The Normal Position: a big center for the pawn.}

lines.name: Accepted 5...Bd6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.b4 Bxb4 5.c3 Bd6 {The Stone-Ware Defense.} 6.d4 Nf6 7.O-O O-O 8.Re1 {A big center.}

lines.name: Compromised Defense 7...dxc3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5 4.b4 Bxb4 5.c3 Ba5 6.d4 exd4 7.O-O dxc3?! {Greedy.} 8.Qb3 Qf6 9.e5 Qg6 10.Nxc3 {A huge lead in development.}

ideas: Punish weakening pawn moves (...f6, ...f5) with direct attacks on the king.
Answer early central counters with quick development and tempo on the queen.
Against the Philidor, keep the center and build space — don't rush.
In the Petrov, avoid copycat tricks: Qe2 pins after 3...Nxe4?

lines.name: Latvian 3...Nc6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 f5?! 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Qh5+ g6 5.Nxg6 Nf6 6.Qh3 hxg6 7.Qxh8 {White wins the exchange.}

lines.name: Elephant 3...e4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d5?! 3.exd5 e4 4.Qe2 Nf6 5.d3 Be7 6.dxe4 O-O 7.Nc3 {Two pawns up.}

lines.name: Philidor Hanham 3...Nd7
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 Nd7 4.Bc4 c6 5.O-O Be7 6.dxe5 dxe5 7.Ng5 {Hitting f7: Black must be precise.}

lines.name: Petrov 6...Bd6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.d4 d5 6.Bd3 Bd6 7.O-O O-O 8.c4 c6 9.Re1 {Hitting the e4 knight.}

lines.name: Stafford 4...bxc6
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 bxc6 5.d3 d5 6.Nd2 Bd6 7.Be2 O-O 8.O-O {White is simply a pawn up.}

ideas: Counter-attack e4 instead of defending passively.
Against Ng5, block with ...d5 and after exd5 play ...Na5 — never ...Nxd5?.
Use the fork trick ...Nxe4 + ...d5 when White's knight on c3 is loose.
Your compensation for a pawn is rapid development and a space-gaining ...e4.

lines.name: 4.Ng5 8.Qf3 Rb8
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Qf3 Rb8 {Activating the rook; Black has strong compensation.}

lines.name: 4.Ng5 9.Nh3 (Steinitz)
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2 h6 9.Nh3 Bc5 10.d3 O-O {Big lead in development.}

lines.name: 4.d4 exd4 5.Ng5?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.Ng5?! d5 6.exd5 Qe7+ {Disrupting White's castling.} 7.Kf1 Ne5 {Black is better.}

ideas: Counter-attack e4 instead of defending e5.
After 3.Nxe5, always kick the knight with ...d6 before taking on e4.
Aim for symmetrical, solid structures and develop harmoniously.
Against sacrifices like Nxf7, accept the piece and walk the king to safety.

lines.name: 5.Qe2 queen trade
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.Qe2 Qe7 6.d3 Nf6 7.Bg5 Qxe2+ 8.Bxe2 Be7 {A level endgame.}

lines.name: 5.d3 quiet
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.d3 Nf6 6.d4 d5 {Symmetrical and comfortable.}

lines.name: 4.Nc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nc4 Nxe4 5.Qe2 Qe7 6.Ne3 Nf6 {Equal.}

ideas: Give the e-pawn for rapid development and open lines toward f2.
The bishop on c5 and a knight on g4 or e4 create threats against f2.
...h5 prepares ...Ng4 and opens the h-file if White plays h3.
Objectively dubious: it works best against natural-looking but careless moves.

lines.name: Trap: 5.Nc3 ...Qd6 idea
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.Nc3 Bc5 6.Be2 h5 7.O-O Ng4 8.h3 Qd6 9.hxg4 hxg4 {Same mating idea: ...Qh2# is threatened.}

lines.name: Trap: 5.e5 Ne4 6.d3? Bc5!
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.e5 Ne4 6.d3? Bc5! {Threatening ...Bxf2+ and ...Nxf2.} 7.dxe4?? Bxf2+! 8.Kxf2 Qxd1 {The queen falls on d1.}

lines.name: 5.d3 Bc5 6.Nc3 Ng4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3 Bc5 6.Nc3 Ng4 7.Be3 Nxe3 8.fxe3 Bxe3 {Pawn regained with the bishop pair.}

ideas: ...a6 controls b5 and prepares ...e5 or ...b5 queenside expansion.
The half-open c-file is Black's highway: rooks and queen go to c8/c7.
In opposite-side castling races, use ...b5-b4 and exchange sacrifices on c3.
...e5 gains space and kicks the d4 knight; then d5 becomes the key square to control.

lines.name: English Attack 7.Nf3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.Be3 e5 7.Nf3 Be7 8.Bc4 O-O 9.O-O Be6 {Trading off White's best bishop.}

lines.name: English Attack 8.Qd2
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.Be3 e5 7.Nb3 Be6 8.Qd2 Nbd7 9.f3 Be7 10.O-O-O O-O {Same race, different move order.}

lines.name: 6.a4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.a4 e5 7.Nf3 Be7 8.Bc4 O-O 9.O-O Be6 {Standard Najdorf structure.}

lines.name: 6.g3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 a6 6.g3 e5 7.Nde2 Be7 8.Bg2 O-O 9.O-O b5 {Queenside expansion.}

lines.name: 3.c3 (beware the Qa4+ trick)
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.c3 Nf6 4.Be2 Nbd7 {Not 4...Nxe4?? 5.Qa4+! winning the knight.} 5.d3 g6 6.O-O Bg7 {Solid.}

lines.name: 3.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Nc6 5.O-O e6 {Blunting the bishop.} 6.c3 Be7 {Comfortable for Black.}

ideas: The g7 bishop is the Dragon's soul — keep it and open the long diagonal.
Counter-attack on the c-file: ...Rc8, ...Ne5-c4 and exchange sacrifices on c3.
Against the Yugoslav Attack, strike back in the center with ...d5 when possible.
Speed is everything in opposite-side castling races.

lines.name: Yugoslav 9.g4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Be3 Bg7 7.f3 O-O 8.Qd2 Nc6 9.g4 Be6 10.Nxe6 fxe6 11.O-O-O Ne5 {Pressure on the f-file and c4.}

lines.name: Yugoslav 9.Bc4 10.h4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Be3 Bg7 7.f3 O-O 8.Qd2 Nc6 9.Bc4 Bd7 10.h4 Rc8 11.Bb3 Ne5 12.O-O-O Nc4 13.Bxc4 Rxc4 {Typical Dragon counterplay.}

lines.name: 6.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Bc4 Bg7 7.O-O O-O 8.Bb3 Nc6 9.Re1 Na5 {Hunting the bishop.}

lines.name: 6.Bg5
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 d6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6 5.Nc3 g6 6.Bg5 Bg7 7.Qd2 Nc6 8.O-O-O Nxd4 9.Qxd4 O-O {Black is fine.}

ideas: Against 2.c3, hit e4 with ...Nf6 at once.
Accepting the Smith-Morra is fine: develop with ...Nc6, ...d6, ...e6 and stop the e5 break.
Versus closed setups, the g7 fianchetto plus ...e5 or ...e6 gives a firm grip on d4.
When White plays dubious gambits, return to the center with ...d5.

lines.name: Alapin 4.Nf3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.Nf3 Nc6 5.Bc4 Nb6 6.Bb3 c4 7.Bc2 Qc7 {Pressure on e5.}

lines.name: Alapin 5.cxd4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.c3 Nf6 3.e5 Nd5 4.d4 cxd4 5.cxd4 d6 6.Nf3 Nc6 7.Bc4 Nb6 8.Bb5 dxe5 9.Nxe5 Bd7 {Same structure, solid for Black.}

lines.name: 2.Nc3 3.Nge2
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Nc3 Nc6 3.Nge2 g6 4.d4 cxd4 5.Nxd4 Bg7 6.Be3 Nf6 {An Accelerated Dragon setup.}

lines.name: 2.d3 King's Indian Attack
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.d3 Nc6 3.g3 g6 4.Bg2 Bg7 5.f4 d6 6.Nf3 e6 {Solid and flexible.}

lines.name: 2.Qh5?! early queen
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.Qh5?! Nf6 {Developing with tempo.} 3.Qh4 Nc6 {Black is already better developed.}

lines.name: Grand Prix 2.f4 d5!
lines.moves: 1.e4 c5 2.f4 d5! {The best answer: opening the center.} 3.exd5 Nf6 4.Bb5+ Bd7 5.Bxd7+ Qxd7 6.c4 e6 {Black regains the pawn with good play.}

ideas: Build the chain e6-d5 and strike its base with ...c5 (and later ...f6).
In the Advance, pile up on d4 with ...Nc6, ...Qb6 and ...Nge7-f5.
Your light-squared bishop is the problem piece: trade it or reroute it.
In the Winawer, ...Bxc3+ doubles White's pawns: counter-attack rather than defend passively.

lines.name: Winawer 4.a3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.a3 Bxc3+ 5.bxc3 dxe4 6.Qg4 Nf6 7.Qxg7 Rg8 8.Qh6 c5 {Black has counterplay for the pawn.}

lines.name: Winawer 4.Ne2
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Bb4 4.Ne2 dxe4 5.a3 Be7 6.Nxe4 Nf6 {Comfortable development.}

lines.name: 2.Nf3 Classical
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.Nf3 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.e5 Nfd7 5.d4 c5 {Hitting the chain.}

lines.name: Exchange 4.c4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.exd5 exd5 4.c4 Bb4+ 5.Nc3 Ne7 6.Nf3 O-O {Pressure on the isolated pawn.}

ideas: Support ...d5 with ...c6 and get the light-squared bishop out before ...e6.
In the Advance, hit the chain with ...c5 and use ...Ne7 and ...Nd7.
In the Classical, the h-pawn duel (h4 ...h6) keeps your bishop safe.
Against isolated-pawn positions (Panov), blockade d5 and trade pieces.

lines.name: Advance 4.Nc3 5.g4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 Bf5 4.Nc3 e6 5.g4 Bg6 6.Nge2 c5 {Striking back in the center.}

lines.name: Advance 4.h4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.e5 Bf5 4.h4 h5 {Stopping h5 and g4 ideas.} 5.c4 e6 6.Nc3 Ne7 {Solid development.}

lines.name: Classical 5.Bd3? Qxd4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5 5.Bd3? Qxd4 {The d4 pawn hangs.} 6.Nf3 Qd8 7.Qe2 Nd7 {Black keeps the pawn.}

lines.name: Accelerated Panov 2.c4
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.c4 d5 3.exd5 cxd5 4.cxd5 Nf6 5.Nc3 Nxd5 {Free development.}

lines.name: 2.d3
lines.moves: 1.e4 c6 2.d3 d5 3.Nd2 e5 {Taking the big center.} 4.Ngf3 Bd6 {Comfortable.}

ideas: Challenge e4 at once; after 2.exd5 Qxd5 the queen is safe on a5.
Develop the light bishop to f5 or g4 before ...e6, then build a ...c6/...e6 triangle.
Don't lose more time with the queen: develop, then castle.
Against gambits, take the material and consolidate.

lines.name: 4.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Qxd5 3.Nc3 Qa5 4.Bc4 Nf6 5.d3 c6 6.Bd2 Qc7 7.Nf3 Bg4 {Comfortable development.}

lines.name: 5.Bd2
